title: Osteoporosis
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Often silent until a fracture. Signs: height loss, increased thoracic kyphosis, sudden back pain after minor stress (vertebral fracture).
qa: What T-score defines osteoporosis? −2.5 or lower.
Which movements should high-risk patients avoid? Repeated loaded spinal flexion with rotation.
Why is resistance training important? It loads bone, builds muscle and reduces falls risk.
What does height loss suggest? Possible vertebral compression fractures.
Why combine balance training? Most hip fractures result from falls.

redFlags.Finding: Sudden severe back pain after minor activity
Hip pain after a fall, unable to weight-bear
Fracture with weight loss, night pain
Back pain with leg weakness or bladder change

manualNotes: Safe movement advice: avoid repeated, loaded, end-range spinal flexion combined with rotation (for example toe touches, sit-ups with twisting, lifting heavy objects with a rounded back) in people with high fracture risk or previous vertebral fractures. Teach hip hinge and neutral spine.
Fear of fracture can make patients avoid all exercise. Inactivity weakens bone and muscle and increases fall risk. Properly prescribed exercise is safe and beneficial.
modalityNotes: Bracing for acute vertebral fractures may help pain in some cases. Medical treatment (bisphosphonates and others), calcium and vitamin D are decided by doctors.
